meta.home: {{BRAND_NAME}}: Knows where you need to be.

areas.title: Timetable
areas.text: Week A and B, double periods, single periods or your own times. {{BRAND_NAME}} shows the current and next lesson with the room.

areas.title: Grades
areas.text: Points from 0 to 15 or grades from 1 to 6, depending on your year. {{BRAND_NAME}} works out each subject's average, exams count a third.

areas.title: Homework and tests
areas.text: Homework, tests and exams with a countdown. Tasks get a due date and one of three priorities.

areas.title: IServ
areas.text: Sign in once with your IServ account. Messages and events then arrive on their own, and on Android your assignments too.

areas.title: Transit
areas.text: Connections with live delays and platforms. The way to school and back home is one tap away.

areas.title: Calendar
areas.text: Your own events, events from IServ and the school holidays and public holidays of all 16 German states, without typing them in.

areas.title: Tinte
areas.text: Tinte is the assistant in {{BRAND_NAME}}. Ask him what is on tomorrow, tell him „Maths p. 38 for Monday“ and he adds the homework. Before an exam he builds you a study plan.

macos: On first launch macOS blocks the app because it isn't signed by Apple. Go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click “Open Anyway”.
steps.macos_terminal: Or paste this into Terminal, the script installs the app into /Applications:
windows: If Windows SmartScreen warns you, click “More info” and “Run anyway”.
{{BRAND_NAME}} installs without admin rights and opens by itself.
linux: Double-click the .deb file to install {{BRAND_NAME}} through your software center, or run this in your Downloads folder: sudo apt install ./{{BRAND_NAME}}-*.deb
Then open {{BRAND_NAME}} from your app menu.
android: Open the APK and allow installs from this source.
{{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when an update is ready.
ios: Tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.
web: Open the link and {{BRAND_NAME}} runs right in your browser.
Your data lives in this browser's storage.

privacy_page.title: What {{BRAND_NAME}} does with your data
privacy_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} has no account and no server of its own for your data. Everything you enter stays on your device. Here is exactly what still goes online and what is encrypted.

where.title: Computer
where.text: In a data folder of your user account, readable only by you.

where.title: Android
where.text: In the app's private storage, other apps can't reach it.

where.title: Web app
where.text: In the browser's storage. Clear the site data and it's gone.

privacy_page.flow_lede: Every connection belongs to a feature. If you don't use the feature, nothing goes out.

flow.what: username and password to sign in, then messages, events, assignments, mail, substitution plan
stops and time of your search, sent to the open transport.rest APIs. On the computer also to Deutsche Bahn for fares
login details and mail, directly via IMAP and SMTP
the term you ask the assistant about
your question to Tinte and the data he needs to answer it
flow.when: only with your own Claude key (computer)

flow.what: addresses of your bookmarks, for the little site icons

privacy_page.lock_text: {{BRAND_NAME}} stores your IServ and mail login details encrypted. On the computer with Fernet and a key from 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds, on Android in the system's encrypted storage. Timetable, tasks and grades are not encrypted, but they only exist on your device.
privacy_page.lock_number_label: PBKDF2 rounds for your login details on the computer
no: No account and no email address
No tracking, no analytics, no crash reports
privacy_page.open_title: You don't have to take my word for it
privacy_page.open_text: {{BRAND_NAME}} is open source under the AGPL-3.0. Every line that touches your data is public on GitHub.

download_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} is still a beta. Free, no account and no ads.

faq.a: No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is free for you and open source under the AGPL-3.0. There are no subscriptions and no paid features.
On Android, the Mac, Windows and Linux, {{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when a new version is out. You download it here.

faq.q: Why isn't {{BRAND_NAME}} in the App Store or on Google Play?
faq.a: I distribute {{BRAND_NAME}} directly, without store fees and with faster updates. That's why the iPhone gets the web app.

faq.q: Can I move my data to a new device?
faq.a: Not yet. There is no cloud and no export so far, your data stays on the device you enter it on.
No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is an independent student project. It only uses your IServ account to sign in on your behalf.
Not yet. The app itself is in German, it was built for German schools.

about_page.title: A student project from Brandenburg.
about_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} is built by a student from Brandenburg, currently in the final years of school. The app started as a tool for their own school day and is now there for anyone looking for something similar.
story: For school, my calendar, the bus and my homework I had a separate app each. None of them knew about the others.
{{BRAND_NAME}} brings that together: the timetable knows which room is next, tests sit with a countdown among your deadlines, and the bus home is one tap away.
Everything runs on your device. I don't want to see your grades, and I can't.

open.title: AGPL-3.0 for everyone
open.text: You may use, read, change and share {{BRAND_NAME}}. If you run a changed version for other people, you have to publish the code for it.

open.title: Licence for schools
open.text: Schools, school authorities and providers who can't publish their changes or need operation with a data processing agreement get a commercial licence.

open.title: Contribute
open.text: Contributions are welcome. They come with a contributor agreement (CLA) that keeps the dual licence possible.

about_page.contact_title: Found a bug or have an idea?
about_page.contact_text: {{BRAND_NAME}} has no automatic crash reports. That's why every message helps right away.

privacy_policy.s2_p1: {{BRAND_NAME}} was built on a "Local-First" principle. This means: All data you enter in the App is stored exclusively on your device. No data is transmitted to servers of the Provider or third parties.

start.agent_text: Tinte is the assistant in {{BRAND_NAME}}. He knows your timetable, your tasks and your grades, adds homework for you and plans with you up to the exam. By default he works entirely on your device.**

chat.text: Tomorrow is an A week. English first in A109, then biology in B214. After the second block you are free.
Done. Maths p. 38 is in your homework, due on Monday.
Can I still make the maths test?
Yes, there are five days until Tuesday. Page 58 tonight, two-way tables tomorrow, tree diagrams at the weekend.

day.text: Good morning. Chemistry in B206 next.
One moment, fetching your homework from IServ.

start.free_lesson: At school they teach you: if an app is free, you are the product.
start.free_text: I get nothing from you, no money and no data. I build {{BRAND_NAME}} for fun and out of conviction: a school app does not belong behind a paywall, and your data belongs neither to advertisers nor to anyone else. It belongs to you. That is why it stays on your device, and not even I can get to it.
